description.main: A slipcased four-volume set on Stage Play, Christopher Williams's theater work first performed at Miller's Studio in Zürich in 2017. It holds the playscript, publicity and research documents, his open letters, essays by Tom McDonough, and an interview with Markus Krajewski.
description.extended:
Stage Play is a slipcased four-volume set on Christopher Williams's theater work of the same name, performed at Miller's Studio in Zürich in May 2017. It publishes the play's script for the first time.

The volumes are Playscript, Supplementary Visual Material, Open Letters, and Essays/Interview. Together they hold documentation of the production, publicity and research material, and the open letters Williams writes to accompany his exhibitions. They also carry two critical essays by Tom McDonough and an interview Williams conducted with the historian Markus Krajewski on the ceramic-tile façades of postwar Cologne. Supplementary Visual Material sets posters and photographs by Williams beside pictures by Zoe Leonard, Dan Graham, and Jeff Wall. Fredi Fischli and Niels Olsen edited the set for gta exhibitions at ETH Zürich, which showed the project from March to June 2017.

Williams was born in Los Angeles in 1956, studied at the California Institute of the Arts, and has been a professor at the Kunstakademie Düsseldorf since 2008. The set is the largest collection of his writing published so far. He restaged the play in 2019 at Frieze New York as Kochgeschirr Adapted for Use, which the later book Kölnische Dramaturgie documents.

notes: Dimensions from Capitain Petzel (241 × 165 × 34 mm); Zwirner and D.A.P. give 6.25 × 9.5 in; Getty 24 cm. Editors Fischli and Olsen from Getty and DNB records (not on Zwirner). Volume page counts per DNB: Playscript 31, Essays/Interview 35, Supplementary Visual Material 75, Open Letters 91 (232 numbered; Zwirner gives 240 total). DNB lists the Open Letters volume language as German; the rest English. Cover is the flat slipcase render used by Zwirner and Capitain Petzel. The twelvebooks photograph of the printed slipcase shows the title panel as maroon rather than the render's olive brown, The colour may differ from the copy in hand. The twelvebooks product handle reads 'stage-play-by-cristina-iglesias' but the page is the Williams book.
